dedupe_keys.name: mastedatabasen existing and planned antenna positions in denmark by service and technology

description: Mastedatabasen is Denmark's public database of antenna positions, set up for transparency about where transmitting antennas are placed; it is run by the Agency for Digital Government, the telecom authority, on base maps from the Danish Agency for Climate Data. It shows existing and planned antenna positions, the area where an antenna is planned, and the service type and technology used at each position. Mobile technologies covered are GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G NR, and further technologies include DAB, DVB-T, FM, fixed wireless access, microwave radio links, land mobile radio services, technology-neutral licences and TV. TETRA positions of the national emergency network SINE are excluded for security reasons, and licence holders without area licences are not included but appear in the frequency register. Positions are plotted from licence holders' coordinates, with an address or a description of the location. Users search by address, region or municipality, filter by service type and technology, and view results on a map or as a list; the database was last updated on 14 July 2026. Coverage: Denmark. Format and access: free web map and list views; no bulk download or API was found on the pages read. Caveats: planned positions may lack addresses; receive-only antennas and TETRA sites are excluded. Simulation uses: locating mobile, broadcast and radio link sites for hazard exposure, and site density for coverage and redundancy analysis. Related records: Tjekditnet gives coverage by address, and the BNetzA and ČTÚ datasets are comparable registers.
